newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Stocks lifted by firm tobacco cos, hi-techs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Stocks lifted by firm tobacco cos, hi-techs.

text.p: U.S. tobacco stocks led most others higher in London on Wednesday, after reports of secret talks over a settlement of the tobacco industry's liabilities.

The Wall Street Journal said Philip Morris Cos and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp were in talks which could lead to the elimination of nearly all the industry's liability, in return for strict advertising curbs and a payment of up to $300 billion over the next 25 years.
Philip Morris stock was trading at $40-1/2, compared with New York's close of $38-7/8. RJR was up US$3/4 at $31.
"The tobaccos are definitely the main excitement for today," said one trader.
The Dow surged 135 points, or 2.1 percent on Tuesday, its best one day advance since 1987. Tame inflation data and solid quarterly earnings had helped to lift sentiment.
"Looking at the bonds and futures, the rally might continue today," a dealer said. "But, we have got the housing starts later and the Dow is very sensitve to economics."
June S&P index futures trading on Globex were down 0.25 points by 1053 GMT.
U.S. housing starts for March at 1230 GMT are expected to total 1.5 million. At 1315 GMT, U.S. industrial production is seen up 0.6 percent and capacity utilisation is seen rising to 83.6 percent.
Among other active stock, hi-techs bounced ahead of a batch of quarterly results from Apple Computer, AMR Corp, Sprint and Compaq Computer on Wednesday.
IBM was trading up $1/2 at $138-3/8 and Texas Instruments was $1/4 better at $84-3/4.
Among the losers Boeing was off $3/8 at $100-1/2. "Boeing has slipped on the threat of the EU spoiling its tie-up with McDonnell Douglas," said a trader.
Shares in WMX Technologies Inc lost $3/8 to $30-1/2 after Moody's Investors Service lowered the debt rating of the company.
